answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity in a cross-cluster attestation quorum: each persona runs a memory-hard kernel rebuilt per clone, so splitting one agent into n identities multiplies compute n-fold. Recognition needs k attestations from disjoint clusters, so no single grove vouches for every fake. Honest clusters sample the kernel before signing and only attest a persona whose haven still matches. Fabricating n identities needs n kernels plus fresh quorums; correlated faults jointly slash that cluster's collateral. Cost is super-linear in identities, non-poolable.
